items.title: COVID Queries: Altered DNA and Microchips
items.snippet_en: Dr. Martin Herrmann of Mayo Clinic Health System states that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and cannot track people or gather personal information. The myth originated from Bill Gates' comments on a digital certificate of vaccine records, not a microchip.

The CDC explicitly states that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips. Vaccines are designed to stimulate the immune system to fight disease, not for tracking purposes. They do not contain preservatives, tissues, antibiotics, food proteins, latex, or metals.
Mayo Clinic reiterates that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips. The vaccines are made only with ingredients that help the body recognize and clear the virus.
Pfizer's website states that no Pfizer vaccine, including the COVID-19 vaccine, contains microchips or any other tracking devices.

Business Insider reports that claims of microchips in COVID-19 vaccines are false and based on misconstrued information. Bill Gates called the conspiracy theory bizarre. The myth may stem from an idea for smart syringe packaging with an optional barcode-like label, not a tracking microchip.

FactCheck.org debunks a video falsely claiming COVID-19 vaccine vials have microchips to track patients. The claim misrepresents an interview about an optional RFID tag on vials to store vaccine dose information, not to track individuals or personal data.
